Lessons.Title: More Arithmetic with Complex Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers, and represent the solutions in the form $a+bi$. Explain reasoning and critique the reasoning of others when writing numbers in the form $a+bi$. Generalize patterns in repeated reasoning to show what happens when $i$ is raised to different powers.
Reduce powers of i modulo 4, apply componentwise addition and subtraction, and distribute for products.

Source activity 14.1: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Complex Expressions: Which one doesn’t belong? B. \((1 + i) + (1 - i)\) D. \((1 + i)(1 - i)\) Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 14.2: Powers of $i$: Write each power of \(i\) in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. If \(a\) or \(b\) is zero, you can ignore that part of the number. For example, \(0+3i\) can simply be expressed as \(3i\). What is \(i^{100}\)? Explain your reasoning. What is \(i^{38}\)? Explain your reasoning. Write each power of \(1+i\) in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 14.3: Add 'Em Up (or Subtract or Multiply): For each row, your partner and you will each rewrite an expression so it has the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. You and your partner should get the same answer. If you disagree, work to reach agreement. Suppose we want to write the product \((3+5i)(7-2i)\) in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. For example, we might want to… Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.
Practice Problem 1: Select all expressions that are equivalent to \(8+16i\). \(\text-2i(\text-8-4i)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 2: Which expression is equivalent to \((\text-4 + 3i)(2-7i)\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 3: Match the equivalent expressions. \(\text-4i \boldcdot 5i\) \((1+2i)(\text-1+3i)\) \((3+5i) - (10+4i)\) \((1-4i) + (\text-4+3i)\) \((\text-6 + 12i) - (\text-21 - 8i)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Write each expression in \(a+bi\) form. \((\text-8 + 3i) - (2 +5i)\) \((3 + 5i)(4 + 3i)\) \((3i)(\text-2 i)(4i)\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Here is a method for solving the equation \(\sqrt{5+x}+10=6\). Does the method produce the correct solution to the equation? Explain how you know. \(\begin{align} \sqrt{5+x}+10 &= 6 \\ \sqrt{5+x} &= \text-4 &\text{ (after subtracting 10 from each side)} \\ 5+x &= 16 &\text{ (after squaring both sides)} \\ x &= 11 \\… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Write each expression in the form \(a+bi\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers. \((4+2i) + (8-2i)\) \(2i \boldcdot 7i\) Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Edulytics independent cool-down: Evaluate i^10. Expected reasoning or answer: -1.
